title: A value that might not be there

prereqs.why: Both functions return an Option, and the three ways of taking one apart are what the problem exercises.
One function returns Option<&String> - a borrow that may not exist - which is where the lifetime annotation comes from.
You have already written the -1 version of this in C++; Option is what replaces it.

statement:
Read `n`, then `n` whitespace-separated names, then `q`, then `q` query strings.
Write these two functions:

```rust
fn find_name<'a>(names: &'a [String], prefix: &str) -> Option<&'a String>
fn position_of(names: &[String], wanted: &str) -> Option<usize>
```

`find_name` returns the **first** name that starts with `prefix`, borrowed from
the list. `position_of` returns the index of the first name **exactly equal** to
`wanted`.

For each query print three lines, using a `match` for the first, an `if let` for
the second, and `map` with `unwrap_or` for the third:

```
prefix <query> <the first name starting with it, or none>
exact <query> <its index, or none>
len <query> <the length of the prefix match, or 0 if there was none>
```

```
input:   3                 output:  prefix ca cache
         cache ring cat              exact ca none
         2                           len ca 5
         ca ring                     prefix ring ring
                                     exact ring 1
                                     len ring 4
```

`ca` is a prefix of `cache` (which comes first) but is not any name exactly, so
its index is `none` and its prefix-match length is 5. Every name is a prefix of
itself, so `ring` matches both ways.

### The point of the problem

In C++ you wrote the same search returning `-1` for "not found", and the
solution noted that this only works because an index cannot be negative. Rust's
answer is to put the absence **in the type**:

```rust
enum Option<T> { Some(T), None }
```

`Option<usize>` is a different type from `usize`. You cannot accidentally use it
as a number, you cannot forget to check it, and there is no value stolen from
the result space - `Option<i64>` can represent every `i64` *and* nothing.

### Three ways to take one apart, and when each fits

```rust
// match: both arms matter
match find_name(&names, query) {
    Some(found) => ...,
    None => ...,
}

// if let: only one arm is interesting
if let Some(i) = position_of(&names, query) { ... } else { ... }

// map + unwrap_or: transform the value if present, substitute a default if not
let len = find_name(&names, query).map(|s| s.len()).unwrap_or(0);
```

Use all three, one per output line, because the shapes are what is being
practised rather than the searching.

### The lifetime annotation, and why only one function needs it

`find_name` returns a reference **into** the list, so the compiler has to know
that the returned borrow is tied to `names` and not to `prefix`. With two
reference parameters it cannot guess, so you say it:

```rust
fn find_name<'a>(names: &'a [String], prefix: &str) -> Option<&'a String>
```

`position_of` returns a `usize`, which borrows nothing, so no annotation is
needed - the elision rules handle it. That contrast is the clearest way to see
what lifetimes are actually for.

### Boundary cases

An empty name list, so every query is `none` and every length 0. A query that
matches nothing. The empty prefix - note that `"".starts_with("")` is true and
every string starts with the empty string, so an empty query matches the first
name. A query matching several names, where only the first counts. Duplicate
names, where `position_of` gives the first index. A query that is a prefix match
but not an exact one, and the reverse is impossible since every name is a prefix
of itself.

### Platform assumptions

Names and queries are non-empty ASCII tokens of at most 40 bytes, except that a
query may be the single character `_`, which the input uses to mean the **empty**
query - the stdin format is whitespace-separated, so an empty token cannot be
written directly. Translate `_` to `""` before searching. `len()` is a byte
length, which equals the character count for ASCII. `n` and `q` are each at most
200.
hints: Return early from the loop: `for n in names { if n.starts_with(prefix) { return Some(n); } } None`. The bare `None` at the end is the value of the function when the loop finishes, so no flag is needed.
`names.iter().enumerate()` gives `(index, &String)` pairs, which is what `position_of` wants. Comparing a `&String` to a `&str` works directly with `==`.

`map` applies a closure to the value inside a `Some` and leaves `None` alone, so `opt.map(|s| s.len())` turns an `Option<&String>` into an `Option<usize>`. `unwrap_or(0)` then supplies the default for the `None` case.

cases.expect:
prefix ca cache
exact ca none
len ca 5
prefix ring ring
exact ring 1
len ring 4

prefix x none
exact x none
len x 0
prefix y none
exact y none
len y 0
